Package nz.ac.wgtn.swen225.lc.app.keybinders

Class ControlKeys

java.lang.Object
nz.ac.wgtn.swen225.lc.app.keybinders.KeyStrokes
nz.ac.wgtn.swen225.lc.app.keybinders.ControlKeys
All Implemented Interfaces:
KeyListener, EventListener
public class ControlKeys extends KeyStrokes implements KeyListener
An extension of the class "KeyStrokes", which is responsible for actually controlling key events, rather than mapping and storing them.

  • Constructor Details

    • ControlKeys

      public ControlKeys(Map<String,Runnable> uiActions)
      When you initialise the "ControlKeys" class, the actions will be bound to their specific keystrokes, and the directions will also be bound to their keystrokes. This is done in two separate methods to separate the two different stages of key assignments.
      Parameters:
      uiActions - A Map of the Actions that will need to be assigned to the certain keys on the keyboard.

    • ControlKeys

      public ControlKeys()
      It is possible to create an instance of "ControlKeys" without loading in the UI Actions; this constructor is only used on its own for the testing of the mappings of keyboard keys to Player Actions.

  • Method Details

    • keyPressed

      public void keyPressed(KeyEvent e)
      When you press a key, you could either be making the player move, or perforDeveloper 4 an action on the GUI. We will first check to see if CTRL is being held down, as this will indicate whether to perform an action that required the CTRL key to be held down. We then check to see if the key pressed is an action, or a direction. Take note for a direction, as one player action is only executed per tick, we will cache the keystroke for the first key pressed. REFERENCE: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/11659801/java-check-if-control-key-is-being-pressed
      Specified by:
      keyPressed in interface KeyListener
      Parameters:
      e - The key that was pressed in the form of a "KeyEvent".
